hypothesis: The tick-RSI reversal adds reversal information beyond the 1.65 profit floor.
variable: profit side of the exit ladder
result: Floor-only beats the RSI path (E -61.24 vs -72.04); removing profit-taking entirely is catastrophic (-131.11). rev_exit_ce 45..70 barely moves expectancy; rev_extreme_ce 65/70/75 are identical.
confidence: Confirmed within this data; 2 sessions, CE only.
decision: RSI reversal reclassified as a delayed profit floor, not an information source.
next: Re-test once the entry side changes; the floor level is the only lever that moved.

hypothesis: A mechanism can tell a temporary pullback from a genuine failure before cutting.
variable: loss side of the exit ladder
result: Pullback tolerance had literally zero effect — at the moment a cut fires price is at its own running low. Fresh-low and structure gating are worse. MFE-aware (-53.54) and realised-ATR x0.75 (-59.77) beat control (-72.04) by tightening for trades that never worked.
decision: Pullback-vs-failure detection from price is closed. Size the stop to whether the trade proved itself instead.
next: Only revisit with a materially different mechanism, not another threshold.

hypothesis: Combining the best profit and loss variants produces a positive-expectancy exit.
result: X6 reached +Rs1.41/trade, PF 1.03, positive on both days and LOO-clean.
confidence: Looked strong on the fitted set — and did not survive EXP-04's fresh entries.

hypothesis: The 3-loss confidence lock destroys opportunity; and the fitted exit variants generalise.
variable: SL-streak gate; exit policy on unseen entries
dataset: 2026-09-04 blocked signals + the same 51 entries as a fresh set
result: Relaxing the lock adds 51 trades and -Rs2,042; removing it adds -Rs1,302. On those same 51 entries X6 fell from +Rs1.41 to -Rs42.33, worse than control; X3 (floor-only + MFE-aware) held at -Rs24.86 vs control -Rs40.05.
confidence: Medium — one session, CE only, upper bound on trade count.
decision: KEEP the SL-streak lock. REJECT X6 as an overfit. X3 remains a candidate, unpromoted.
next: Re-price both once real spreads exist; X6's edge died above a 0.36% round trip.

hypothesis: The entry signal selects better-than-arbitrary moments inside its own active windows.
control: arbitrary CE entries on a grid
result: Active-window design: -Rs72.04 vs -Rs8.58, randomisation p=0.0235. Whole-day design: gap -Rs48.63, p=0.1434. Signal-true vs signal-absent: p=0.2082.
confidence: WEAKENED to suggestive. Design-sensitive, p ranges 0.02-0.21 at n=24.
decision: No evidence of positive selection value; not established as negative either.
next: Repeat once several post-repair sessions exist.

hypothesis: Some scoring component discriminates between better and worse moments.
treatment: each component's high vs low bucket
result: 8 of 12 score sub-components and 7 of 17 confidence sub-components are constant on every row. Only two distinct (score, confidence) pairs per day. Every varying component points the wrong way; only the strategy's own RSI is right-signed and it still loses to the benchmark.
confidence: High for the structural counts; low for the directional readings.
decision: Do not tune weights. Fix the inputs first.
next: Re-measure variance after the delta/OI repair.

hypothesis: The dead components are dead because their tick inputs were never populated.
result: broker.py never set atr, delta, oi, open_interest or greeks. One unset delta key pinned BOTH delta(10) and greeks(5) to zero; oi unset pinned oi(10) and oi_score. Populated delta lands in the scorer's band on 82.3% of instants and adds up to 14.3 points of score range. Exposed a second defect: PE deltas are negative and the scorer compared unsigned, so every PE scored zero.
confidence: Confirmed in code and data. Performance effect unproven — the measured gain came from one strike on one day.
decision: Repairs merged behind flags, defaults off; flags enabled in .env for the next session.
next: Attribute gate effect vs ranking effect after that session.

hypothesis: The unscored pre-filters block instants that would have lost.
control: arbitrary CE entries on a 30s grid (E=-Rs31.50)
treatment: entering anyway at each pre-filter's rejected instants
result: Chop filter p=0.116, CE block p=0.157, PE block p=0.305 — none separated. Time filter costly: +Rs57.96. Follow-up: the 09:15-09:45 window it blocked returns +Rs114.06/trade vs -Rs34.41 for 09:45-15:10, permutation p=0.0057, positive on all three sessions, +Rs47.09 after dropping the strongest day.
confidence: Medium-high for the window effect; the other gates are unresolved, not cleared.
decision: Time gate already opened for the next session, which becomes the out-of-sample test. Chop filter and directional blocks: no action, insufficient evidence either way.
next: Re-run on the first session that trades the opening; re-check under real spreads.

hypothesis: Losing entries enter high in their own 1-minute candle.
result: Completed-candle version: winners 41.6% vs losers 68.9%, exact permutation p=0.0042, replicating on both days. Causal versions all collapse: partial-bar p=0.54, trailing-60s p=0.53, trailing-180s p=0.66, previous completed bar p=0.094.
confidence: RETRACTED — a look-ahead artifact. The completed bar contains post-entry ticks, so a losing trade lowers its own bar's low.
decision: Withdrawn. The research layer now builds entry bars from ticks up to the entry second only, with a regression test.
next: None. Kept as the reason the as-of rule is enforced structurally.

hypothesis: dvf_trades is a larger research sample.
result: 2,639 of 2,642 rows have no slippage model; every exit reason is a virtual rule and none of the real exit ladder appears; median hold 1,800s against 25s; longest 56 days (a restart artifact); 34% have exactly zero P&L; the mix is PE-dominated where real trades are CE-dominated.
confidence: High — direct counts over the full table.
decision: REJECTED as a research sample. Excluded from every chart and kept visually separate.
next: Use the replay lab if a larger sample is wanted.
